explain.en: We make the past passive with was / were + the past participle. Use was with a singular subject and were with a plural subject.
explain.ar: نكوّن المبني للمجهول في الماضي بـ was / were + التصريف الثالث للفعل (اسم المفعول). نستخدم was مع المفرد و were مع الجمع.

explain.en: We use the passive when the action is more important than the person who did it, or when we do not know who did it. We use by + agent only if it is important.
explain.ar: نستخدم المبني للمجهول عندما يكون الحدث أهم من الفاعل أو عندما لا نعرف الفاعل. نضيف by + الفاعل فقط إذا كان مهمًّا.

grammar.title: Second Conditional (If + past simple, would + infinitive)

explain.en: We use the second conditional to talk about imaginary or unlikely situations in the present or future: If + past simple, would + infinitive.
explain.ar: نستخدم الجملة الشرطية الثانية للحديث عن مواقف خيالية أو غير محتملة في الحاضر أو المستقبل: If + الماضي البسيط، would + المصدر.

explain.title: Form
rows: If I lived in ancient Egypt,
I would see the pyramids being built.

explain.en: After if we can use were for all persons: If I were a king, ... / If he were an architect, ... The result clause can come first: I would travel to Rome if I had a ticket.
explain.ar: بعد if يمكن استخدام were مع جميع الضمائر: If I were a king. يمكن أن تأتي جملة النتيجة أولًا دون فاصلة: I would travel to Rome if I had a ticket.

explain.title: Questions and short answers
rows: What would you do if you found an ancient coin?
I would give it to a museum.
Would you visit Egypt if you had the chance?
Yes, I would. / No, I wouldn't.
If you were an archaeologist, where would you work?

items.en: If I were an emperor, I would build schools for everyone.

items.en: If we had a time machine, we would visit ancient Rome.

items.en: She wouldn't be tired if she slept early.

items.ar: ماذا ستفعل لو اكتشفت مدينة مفقودة؟

explain.en: Do not use would in the if clause: If I had a boat, I would sail. (NOT If I would have a boat). The second conditional is not about real plans; for real possibilities use the first conditional (If it rains, we will stay home).
explain.ar: لا نستخدم would بعد if مباشرة. الشرطية الثانية لا تتحدث عن خطط حقيقية؛ أما الاحتمالات الواقعية فنستخدم معها الشرطية الأولى (If + مضارع، will + مصدر).

items.en: Salalah is famous for its frankincense.
The students are interested in learning about the Sumerians.
The king was proud of his strong fleet.
Who is responsible for this museum?

explain.en: Surprised at / amazed at have the same meaning. Different from is correct in British English (different to is also used). Do not translate the Arabic preposition word for word: interested IN (not interested of), scared OF.
explain.ar: surprised at و amazed at لهما المعنى نفسه. لا نترجم حرف الجر حرفيًّا من العربية، فنقول interested in وليس interested of، و scared of.

items.q: Omar is interested [[1]] collecting old coins.
My sister is brilliant [[2]] solving puzzles.
Many people were involved [[3]] the search for the lost ship.

Who is responsible [[5]] cleaning the classroom today?
I wasn't surprised [[6]] the result because he had studied hard.
We are very sorry [[7]] losing your book.
The team was delighted [[8]] winning the cup.
Please be kind [[9]] new students.

exercises.title: Exercise 2 — Complete with the correct preposition

items.q: The little girl is scared ________ the dark.
Egypt is famous ________ its ancient pyramids.
We were amazed ________ the beauty of the temple.
Are you bored ________ this long film?
He is proud ________ his grandfather, who was a sailor.
The old bag was stuffed ________ clay tablets.
She is great ________ painting pictures of forts.
Life in ancient times was very different ________ life today.
Many people were involved ________ building the dam.
The teacher was sorry ________ the mistake on the board.

lines.text: Noor, are you interested [[1]] the history of Oman?

lines.text: Yes, very much. I am proud [[2]] my country's long history.
